subject.title: Apply design-system composer to app chat UI

question: Should the Windows app adopt this design-system composer now and move the speech/tool-call controls into Settings as part of the same change?
rationale: The branch combines a substantial chat interaction redesign with a new persisted preference and control relocation while the foundational design-system PR remains open, so implementation correctness alone cannot establish the intended product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the combined direction
options.body: Approve the composer redesign plus Settings relocation, then require translations, conflict resolution, focused validation, and current-head visual proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to composer styling
options.body: Keep existing control ownership and behavior while landing only the approved visual composer changes in a smaller PR.

options.title: Wait for the design-system seed
options.body: Pause this PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/962 establishes the reusable pattern and review expectations.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the combined direction
recommendation.body: Approve the composer redesign plus Settings relocation, then require translations, conflict resolution, focused validation, and current-head visual proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing candidate for a Windows Hub product-level UI decision, though the file-specific ownership trail is incomplete.
